basis: Intellectual disability and Hirschsprung disease define the syndrome; congenital heart abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Genital anomalies and incontinence do not establish renal damage.
Skin/nail, limb and dental defects define ADULT syndrome; nasolacrimal duct obstruction occurs in 80-99%.
Disease located in the ciliary body of the eye; the umbrella does not imply an immune mechanism.
Thoracic/skeletal and external-ear malformations define the syndrome. Frequencies of cleft palate, ptosis and ventricular septal defect are unspecified.
Skeletal-muscle chloride channelopathy causing myotonia and hypertrophy; no primary nerve or neuromuscular-junction disease.
Poorly defined adult non-neuronopathic sphingolipidosis; available evidence does not establish frequencies of functional visceral organ damage.
Brain malformations and developmental delay define the neurologic component. Reported genitourinary findings are predominantly reproductive, without established renal damage.
Defined by congenital esophageal shortening, intrathoracic stomach and vertebral defects; pulmonary damage is not established as a common intrinsic manifestation.
Neoplasm occupying the pericardium.
Autoinflammation, arthritis and vasculitis define disease; seizures 3/3 and developmental impairment 2/4 support neurologic damage. Anemia 3/4 omitted by cap; renal/skin data sparse.
Nematode infection umbrella with variable intestinal, muscular, renal and other tissue targets; no additional damaged organ is established across the group.
Neuronal migration disorder with heterotopic gray matter; associated skull/ethmoid bone defects and encephaloceles are frequent (30-79%).
Acetyl-CoA transport defect with neurodegeneration and cataracts; hearing impairment occurs in 5/5 patients.
Protein-losing hypertrophic gastropathy confined to gastric mucosa; associated H. pylori infection is separate, and hypoalbuminemia does not establish another damaged organ.
Malignant osteoid-producing tumor arising in bone. Potential pulmonary metastases do not establish common intrinsic lung involvement.
Central movement disorder, sometimes accompanied by neurodevelopmental impairment; abnormal tone does not establish primary skeletal-muscle damage.
Focal dystonia producing involuntary upward eye deviation; the movement abnormality does not indicate damage to the eye.
Muscular dystrophy with conduction defects and cataracts (80-99%); cognitive impairment occurs in 30-79%. Endocrine deficits listed are 5-29%; baldness omitted by cap.
Skeletal dysplasia with congenital joint dislocations. Hearing impairment 4/19 and cleft palate 5-29% fall below the involvement threshold.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis in 5/6; middle-ear clearance dysfunction causes recurrent otitis in 6/6. Situs inversus alone does not imply organ damage.
Structural pituitary-gland disorder, sometimes with hormone deficiencies; no common direct brain or ocular damage is established.
Localized hair-follicle anomaly, sometimes with epidermal nevi; ocular and ear anomalies occur in 5-29%, and precocious puberty in 1-4%.
Neurodevelopmental and hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction define PWS; scoliosis and strabismus each occur in 30-79%. Respiratory infections do not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Inherited marrow disorder with erythroid and granulocytic hypoplasia, anemia and neutropenia in 2/2 patients.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability predominate across 22q duplication subtypes; other organ malformations vary with the duplicated interval.
